figures.finding: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba (Caribbean Netherlands) have their own tax laws (the BES acts), not the European Netherlands' tax: a resident pays a combined wage/income tax of 29.4% on taxable income up to USD 53,198 and 38.4% above, after a tax-free amount of USD 21,956 (2026); the employee's AOV/AWW and health premiums are inside the 29.4% by way of credits.
figures.applies: 2026. The handbook's summary table gives the band edge as USD 51,251 but its rate table as USD 53,198; the rate table is used.

sources.said: Loonbelasting (bij een belastbare som van niet meer dan USD 51.251) 29,4% Loonbelasting (bij een belastbare som van meer dan USD 51.251) 38,4%
In 2026 bedraagt de belastingvrije som USD 21.956.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; the 2025 income tax return was due by 18 May 2026.
figures.applies: 2026 return due in 2027 on a date set yearly.

sources.said: De aangifte Inkomstenbelasting 2025 moet uiterlijk 18 mei 2026 zijn ingediend.

figures.finding: The employee pays AOV 25.0%, AWW 1.3% and health insurance 0.5% on pay up to USD 38,390 (2026), credited inside the 29.4% combined levy; the employer pays ZV 0.7%, OV 0.2%, cessantia 0.1% and health insurance 9.3%.

sources.said: Premie AOV 25,0% Premie AWW 1,3% Premie ZV 0,7% Premie OV 0,2% Premie CES 0,1% Premie Zorgverzekering 0,5% 9,3%
maximum premiegrondslag. In 2026 is dat USD 38.390.

figures.finding: The employer withholds the combined wage tax and premiums from pay, by period tables; with no valid wage-tax statement it applies the anonymous rate.

sources.said: De loonheffing dient u in te houden op het loon van de werknemer.

figures.finding: A non-resident performer engaged without a contract of service is in a deemed employment and has 10% wage tax withheld by the payer; a non-resident gets no tax-free amount.

Hoofdregel is dat de werknemer die niet op een van de BES-eilanden woont geen recht heeft op de belastingvrije som

figures.finding: There is no VAT; general expenditure tax (ABB) on services is 6% on Bonaire and 4% on Sint Eustatius and Saba.
